sourceFacts.fact: Assessment of suspected late-onset neonatal sepsis particularly includes consideration of lumbar puncture and meningitis.
CSF assessment can identify CNS infection; LP safety must be assessed, and urgent antibiotics must not be delayed in a seriously unwell child.

layoutSpecification: Title 'Late-onset neonatal sepsis'. A branching evaluation concept with a small fully wrapped sleeping-infant pictogram at LEFT above caption 'Think beyond the bloodstream'. Two parallel large branches go RIGHT. TOP branch ends at a small closed specimen tube with muted red fluid labelled 'Blood assessment'. LOWER branch goes to a large question-mark token labelled 'Consider meningitis', then to a second closed specimen tube with CLEAR pale-blue fluid labelled 'CSF assessment when safe'. No brain, spinal cord, meninges, body compartments, needle placement, microbes or lab microscope view. The tubes are specimen symbols, not diagnostic appearance. Bottom bold short line 'Urgent treatment must not wait'. No claim all late sepsis has meningitis or that early sepsis excludes it.
